title: Recombinant Rabies Virus Titration by Quantitative PCR
author: Zhang, Gao, et al.
materials: PowerUp SYBR green master mix for qPCR

steps.title: Coat plates with poly‑L‑lysine
steps.instruction: Apply 3 mL of 0.01 % poly‑L‑lysine (1:6 diluted in 1× DPBS) to each 10 cm plate, let stand 1 h in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator, gently agitating to spread evenly.

steps.title: Seed cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate the coating solution, resuspend 6 × 10⁶ cells in 8 mL DMEM containing 10 % FBS and 1 % antibiotic‑antimycotic, seed onto the coated 10 cm plate, and incubate 18–24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to reach ~80 % confluence.

steps.title: Prepare transfection mix
steps.instruction: Dilute the required plasmids (0.5–2 µg/µL each; amounts per Tables 2‑3) in 1.5 mL Opti‑MEM and mix thoroughly. In a separate tube dilute 72 µL Lipofectamine 2000 in 1.5 mL Opti‑MEM, incubate ~25 °C 5 min. Combine DNA and Lipofectamine 1:1, incubate ~25 °C 20 min.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells with 3 mL DPBS and replace with 5 mL Opti‑MEM.
Add the DNA‑Lipofectamine mixture dropwise to the cells and agitate to distribute evenly.
After 5–6 h replace the medium with 10 mL fresh DMEM.

steps.title: Collect first viral supernatant (72 h)
steps.instruction: Label a 15 mL tube “VirusName_Sup1”. Collect all supernatant (~8–9 mL) carefully, replace the medium with 7 mL fresh DMEM, spin at 2000 rpm (724 g) 5 min, filter through a 0.45 µm membrane, retain 200 µL for titering, store the remaining supernatant and the 200 µL aliquot at –20 °C (short‑term) or –80 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Collect daily supernatants
steps.instruction: Collect supernatant each day for 5 days (or every 2 days until Day‑13 for CVS‑N2cΔG) and repeat the collection, spin, filter, and storage steps as above, yielding six aliquots total.

steps.title: Thaw pooled supernatants
steps.instruction: Keep the harvested supernatants at 4 °C for 18–24 h to thaw completely, then pool all supernatants into a 150 mL bottle.

steps.title: Warm pooled supernatant
steps.instruction: Place the pooled, filtered supernatant at ~25 °C for at least 1 h.

steps.title: Benzonase treatment
steps.instruction: Add Benzonase to a final concentration of 30 U/mL and incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Prepare 25 % sucrose cushion
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6 g sucrose in 24 mL DPBS (1×) at 37 °C, let stand 1 h, then filter through a 0.22 µm membrane to obtain 25 % (w/v) sucrose solution.

steps.title: Load ultracentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 33 mL of the Benzonase‑treated supernatant into each of four conical‑bottom ultracentrifuge tubes and underlay each with 5 mL 25 % sucrose using a long cannula and a 10 mL syringe.

steps.title: Ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Set the ultracentrifuge to 4 °C, balance the buckets, and spin at 22 000 rpm (82 700 × g) using an SW 32 Ti rotor for 2 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Recover virus pellet
steps.instruction: Quickly invert the tubes, discard the supernatant, pipette off any remaining droplets, and resuspend each pellet in 18 µL cold 1× DPBS.

steps.title: Overnight shake
steps.instruction: Place the four tubes on a 50 mL rack and shake in a cold room (4 °C) on a flat shaker for 18–24 h.

steps.title: Combine concentrates
steps.instruction: Transfer the four 18 µL virus suspensions into a single 1.5 mL tube, keep on ice.

steps.title: Decontaminate equipment
steps.instruction: Clean the used centrifuge tubes, buckets, conical adaptors, and rack with 75 % ethanol and discard the four original tubes.

steps.title: Aliquot concentrated virus
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, place cryogenic tubes on a cold rack, loosen caps, gently pipet the virus up and down several times, spin at 1000 rpm for 1 min to remove froth, aliquot 5 µL per tube, label “VirusName‑P1‑Date”, and freeze immediately at –80 °C.

steps.title: FACS titration of concentrated virus
steps.instruction: Prepare the dilution series shown in Table 5 (Dil.0‑4) using culture medium, add the appropriate volume of virus to each dilution, and perform FACS titration as described in the manuscript.

steps.title: Prepare plasmid standards
steps.instruction: Transform the plasmid used for the standard curve, culture a single colony, extract plasmid with a kit eluting in TE buffer, measure concentration with a NanoDrop, dilute to 20–50 ng/µL with TE, determine the average concentration from three readings, aliquot 10 µL into 0.2 mL PCR tubes, store aliquots at –20 °C and the remaining stock at –80 °C.

steps.title: Extract viral RNA
steps.instruction: Retrieve 5 µL purified virus from –80 °C, thaw on ice, bring volume to 200 µL with RNase‑free water, add 200 µL Buffer VGB, 20 µL Proteinase K, and 1 µL Carrier RNA, mix and incubate 56 °C 10 min; add 200 µL 96–100 % ethanol, mix, transfer to a spin column, centrifuge 12 000 rpm 2 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash RNA column
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer RWA, centrifuge 12 000 rpm 1 min, discard; add 700 µL Buffer RWB, centrifuge 12 000 rpm 1 min, discard; repeat the Buffer RWB wash once more; finally centrifuge 12 000 rpm 2 min to dry the membrane.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Place the column in a new 1.5 mL RNase‑free tube, add 32 µL RNase‑free water to the membrane center, stand 5 min at room temperature, then centrifuge 12 000 rpm 2 min; store the eluted RNA at –80 °C.

steps.title: DNase I treatment
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL PCR tube combine 16 µL RNA, 0.2 µL Recombinant DNase I (25 U/µL) to give 0.2 U/µL, 0.4 µL RNase Inhibitor (0.540 U/µL) to give 0.4 U/µL, 1 µL 10× DNase buffer, and RNase‑free water to a final volume of 26.5 µL; mix and incubate as recommended (e.g., 37 °C 15 min).

steps.title: Optional ethanol precipitation
steps.instruction: If needed, bring the RNA solution to 100 µL with RNase‑free water, add 10 µL 3 M sodium acetate and 250 µL cold 96–100 % ethanol, mix, incubate at ≤‑80 °C for ≥20 min, centrifuge 15 000 rpm at 4 °C for 25 min, discard supernatant, wash the pellet with cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 12 000 rpm at 4 °C for 5 min, discard, air‑dry ~10 min, and resuspend in 16 µL RNase‑free water.
